title: Exact zero modes in interacting Majorana X- and Y-junctions
authors: Bowy M La Rivière, Rik Mulder and Natalia Chepiga
abstract: We report the emergence of exact zero modes (EZMs) in junctions of two, three and four short interacting Majorana wires, equivalent to a chain with an impurity bond, Y- and X- junctions respectively. These EZMs arise from incommensurate short-range correlations and manifest as exact level crossings between in-gap states upon continuously tuning the interaction strength. In a junction of two chains the EZMs and parity switching appear as soon as the coupling across a junction is positive. This conclusion has a broad implication including the existence of EZM in quench- disordered systems. Remarkably, for junctions with multiple chains the in-gap states group up into sets of parity pairs–pairs of quasi-degenerate states with opposite parity attributed to the effective interaction of the outer edges of the junction. In the Y-junction with four in-gap states, we report EZMs not only within each parity pair but also between them. We demonstrate that this is attributed to an additional Majorana fermion localized at the center of the junction and protected by fermion parity symmetry. Therefore, coupling between the Majorana fermions at the outer edges of the junction is mediated by the central one. We argue that this is a generic feature of junctions with an odd number of arms. Surprisingly, in the X-junction we identify eight in-gap states arising from two Majorana degrees of freedom localized at the junction center. In contrast to the Y-junction, however, we show that the emergence of Majorana modes at the center of the X-junction is not topologically protected. As a result, the system parameters can be tuned such that the Majorana modes are expelled from the junction center and remain localized exclusively at the outer edges of the system.

title: Photoelectron spectroscopy with a resonant dichromatic field: role of geometric phase
authors: Evan Munaro-Langloÿs, Axel Stenquist and Jan Marcus Dahlström
abstract: We investigate geometric-phase control in resonantly driven two-level atoms exposed to near-degenerate dichromatic laser pulses. In contrast to conventional two-colour schemes based on widely separated frequencies, the closely spaced frequency components generate a slowly varying beating envelope that repeatedly reverses the pseudo-spin rotation on the Bloch sphere. This enables coherent control of the geometric phase accumulated during Rabi dynamics and strongly modifies the resulting photoelectron spectra. Using an exactly solvable model for flat-top pulse envelopes, we derive the essential-state dynamics analytically and analyse photoionization induced both by an auxiliary field and by the dichromatic driving field itself. We show that the formation of Autler–Townes (AT) doublets can be interpreted in terms of destructive interference associated with geometric phases acquired during completed pseudo-spin rotations. Beyond the canonical AT regime, beat-induced reversal dynamics lead to qualitatively different spectral structures, including re-emergent central peaks and higher-order sidebands. These effects originate from the nonuniform temporal evolution induced by the beating envelope, which modifies the balance between positive and negative excitation amplitudes. Our results establish beating-field control as a route toward engineering geometric-phase interference in ultrafast light–matter interactions and suggest broader applications in coherent control of atoms, molecules, and x-ray-driven systems.

title: Charged Bose polarons at finite momentum
abstract: Charged impurities in quantum fluids have unveiled new classes of strongly correlated many-body states across condensed matter, ultracold gases, and hybrid atom–ion platforms. While previous studies have primarily focused on their ground-state and static properties, much less is known about their finite-momentum behavior, which governs transport, dissipation, and quasiparticle stability. Here, we investigate the momentum-dependent properties of a charged Bose polaron using a diagrammatic approach within second-order perturbation theory, explicitly accounting for the finite-range nature of the ion–atom interaction. We show that the interaction range introduces a characteristic momentum scale at which many-body dressing and dissipation are maximized, leading to a non-monotonic behavior of the damping rate and quasiparticle energy. In the high-momentum regime, we uncover a scaling law , signaling the suppression of many-body dressing and the recovery of quasi-free impurity dynamics, in stark contrast to the divergent behavior predicted by contact-interaction perturbative treatments.

title: Multipath wave–particle duality with exact quantification of which-path knowledge
authors: L F Melo, O Jiménez and L Neves
abstract: A quantum system (quanton) traverses an interferometer with equally probable paths and interacts with another quantum system (detector) that stores path information in a set of symmetric states. In this interferometric framework, we present a systematic quantitative study of wave–particle duality based on entropic trade-off relations between quantum coherence, characterized by the relative entropy of coherence of the quanton state, and which-path knowledge, quantified by the mutual information obtained through detector-state discrimination. Unlike prior upper-bound-based formulations, we obtain an exact quantification of which-path knowledge for the discrimination strategies considered here, encompassing previously considered strategies and extending beyond them. A general optimal measurement achieving this is implemented through a state-separation map governed by a continuous parameter , followed by minimum-error (ME) discrimination of either the successful outputs only (standard approach) or both the successful and failure outputs (concatenated approach). Our framework identifies a strategy-dependent hierarchy that generally emerges in the tightness of the resulting duality relations. At , both approaches reduce to the ME measurement, which typically yields the tightest relation. For , each approach yields a distinct relation that generally becomes less tight as increases, with the concatenated strategy always yielding a relation at least as tight as its standard counterpart. We further characterize the saturation of these relations by identifying the sets of detector states that lead to it and show that nontrivial saturation occurs only for interferometers with a nonprime number of paths. From these saturating sets, we elucidate how the underlying structure of the quanton-detector correlations gives rise to this behavior and explains the lack of universal saturation in multipath duality relations for pure states.

title: Magnetic-field-induced nondipole effect in strong field frustrated double ionization
authors: Linna Zhang, Mingzheng Wei, Luling Jin, Huipeng Kang and Xiaojun Liu
abstract: Strong field atomic frustrated double ionization (FDI) represents a novel approach for ultrafast preparation and control of highly excited ions. A comprehensive understanding of its mechanism is of fundamental significance. However, current interpretations are restricted to the dipole approximation. Here, the nondipole effect in FDI of Ar is investigated using a classical ensemble model, in which the magnetic component of the laser field is fully accounted for. We show that the magnetic field induces positive momentum of photoelectrons along the laser propagation direction, which depends on the laser intensity. By tracing the electron trajectories, it is found that the linear momentum transfer to photoelectrons is considerably enhanced by recollision. The ionization time distribution of electrons and corresponding momenta play important roles in the momentum transfer. The subcycle evolution of magnetic fields is related to the variation of momentum transfer for positive and negative momentum of photoelectrons along the laser polarization. This work provides an intuitive insight into the nondipole effect in FDI and offers a scheme for probing ultrafast magnetic fields and manipulating the linear momentum transfer.

title: Bright, directional electron emission from nanowire coated targets under petawatt, femtosecond irradiation
authors: Ameya Parab, Jian Fuh Ong, Stefania Ionescu, Sagar Dam, Sk Rakeeb, Hideaki Habara, Rudrajyoti Palit, Daniel Popa, Deepak Sangwan, Klaus Spohr, Lucian Tudor, Adrian Vatcu, K Yamanaka, Prashant Kumar Singh, Kazuo A Tanaka and G Ravindra Kumar
abstract: Nanostructured targets have long been explored for controlling laser absorption and particle acceleration, but whether they survive the pre-pulse of a petawatt-class laser at realistic temporal contrast remains an open question. We report an experimental and simulation study of nickel nanowire-coated targets irradiated by the ELI-NP 1-PW laser without a plasma mirror. At the built-in contrast of the nanowires increase the relativistic electron flux and redistribute the emission direction. The effect is angle dependent, where at the cutoff energy rises from – MeV relative to a flat foil, whereas along the laser axis ( ) the flat target retains the higher cutoff. Three-dimensional simulations reproduce this redistribution and attribute it to the quasi-static azimuthal magnetic field driven by the return current along the wires.

title: Single photon zeptosecond interferometry
authors: Geoffrey R Harrison, Tobias Saule, R Esteban Goetz, George N Gibson, Camilo Granados, Bikash K Das, Marcelo F Ciappina, Anh-Thu Le and Carlos A Trallero-Herrero
abstract: We demonstrate the generation of a train of attosecond XUV pulses that are in a superposition of wavefront states. Such superposition yields a high precision, self-referencing, common path XUV interferometer setup to produce pairs of spatially separated and independently controllable XUV pulses that are locked in phase and time with a temporal jitter of 3.5 zs (zs = zeptoseconds = s ). In our approach, we can independently control the relative phase/delay of the two optical beams with a resolution of 52 zs. Since the jitter is on the order of the Compton time scale , we explore the level of correlation between the non-local photons by comparing different spatial mode superpositions. Further, thanks to the stability of the interferometer we can retrieve the interference pattern through photon counting. Through post-selection of different particle events we can analyze one, two or more photon events. We argue that this zeptosecond level of temporal precision will open the door for new dynamical quantum electrodynamics (QED) tests at lower intensities while photon counting experiments can also have an impact on the emerging field of quantum light in strong fields. We also discuss the potential impact on other areas, such as time-dependent QED, imaging, measurements of non-locality, and molecular quantum tomography.

title: Spin Seebeck effect under periodic heating: three-temperature approach
authors: A I Bezuglyj and L N Davydov
abstract: Within the framework of the phenomenological three-temperature approach, we considered the dynamics of the temperatures of electrons, phonons and magnons in a layered heterostructure consisting of a thin film of normal metal (NM), a layer of ferromagnetic insulator (FI) and a massive dielectric substrate. The dependence of the constant and variable components of the inverse spin Hall effect voltage on the thickness of the FI during periodic heating of the NM was obtained. From the agreement between the theoretical results obtained and experiments on Pt/YIG heterostructures, the values of a number of parameters characterizing the interaction of electrons and phonons with magnons were found.

title: Channel formation enhances target consumption by chemotactic active Brownian particles
authors: Vladimir Yu Rudyak, Shahar Shinehorn and Yael Roichman
abstract: In many situations, simply finding a target during a search is not enough. It is equally important to be able to return to that target repeatedly or to enable a larger community to locate and utilize it. While first passage time is commonly used to measure search success, relatively little is known about measures of repeated target encounters, such as the mean first passage count, and their rate over time. Here we compare an active Brownian particle model with central resetting, with and without chemotaxis. Searchers with no individual memory but shared environmental memory encode information about the target’s location in the environment, outperforming purely memoryless strategies by boosting the overall hit rate. We further show that this approach leads to a sublinear dependence of encounter rate on target size, reducing the impact of target size on a successful search and increasing the total utilization time of the target.

title: Piston control in a two-ion quantum device
authors: Jing Li, E Ya Sherman and Andreas Ruschhaupt
abstract: We propose a scheme for piston control in a two-ion quantum device with motion confined to orthogonal axes. In this system, one ion plays the role of a ‘classical’ piston driven by the Coulomb interaction with the other ion, whose quantum motion is controlled through modulation of its trapping potential. The stationary state is determined self-consistently, taking quantum effects into account. We identify a narrow quantum regime of the ground state connecting two broad classical regimes. We further design inverse-engineering protocols to control the motion of the ‘classical’ ion. The proposed control scheme provides a useful route toward controlled piston dynamics in microscopic quantum devices.
